 Key points
 About 11.4 lakh non-gazetted railway employees get 78 days' bonus — up to ₹17,951. 
 Postal staff, Gramin Dak Sevaks and ESIC's Group C staff get 60 days — ₹13,816. 
 Other central Group C and non-gazetted Group B staff get a 30-day ad-hoc bonus — ₹6,908. 
 Every bonus is worked out on a ₹7,000 monthly ceiling, so actual pay does not change the amount. 
 Advertisement
 New Delhi, 24 October: The Diwali bonus has reached central government employees this month — but not in equal measure. A railway pointsman can take home up to ₹17,951, a postal MTS ₹13,816, and a Group C clerk in a ministry ₹6,908. Their salaries are not far apart. Their bonuses are more than two and a half times apart.
 The gap has nothing to do with pay. It comes from two things: how many days of bonus each group gets, and the ₹7,000 ceiling that every bonus is calculated on. Four government orders between 14 and 17 October set out the full picture.
 Who got how much
 Who Days of bonus Maximum amount 
 Non-gazetted railway employees (about 11.4 lakh) 78 days ₹17,951 
 Postal MTS, Group C and non-gazetted Group B 60 days ₹13,816 
 Gramin Dak Sevaks (GDS) 60 days ₹13,816 
 ESIC Group C employees 60 days ₹13,816 
 Other central Group C and non-gazetted Group B (incl. eligible CAPF and Armed Forces) 30 days ₹6,908 
 Casual labour, Department of Posts 60 days ₹2,368 
 Casual labour, other departments 30 days ₹1,184 
 The Cabinet approved the railway bonus on 14 October , the Finance Ministry’s order came on 15 October , the Department of Posts followed on 16 October and ESIC on 17 October .
 Why the same bonus whatever the salary?
 Every order works the bonus out on ₹7,000 a month, however much more an employee actually earns. The lowest basic pay at the Centre is ₹18,000, and 60% DA is added to it, so almost every employee is above the ceiling — which is why staff on very different salaries in the same department get the same bonus.
 The sum is simple: ₹7,000 divided by 30.4 gives one day’s bonus, multiplied by the number of days. For 30 days that is ₹6,908; for 60 days, ₹13,816.
 Why 78 days for Railways but 30 for others?
 In the Railways, the Department of Posts and ESIC, the bonus is “productivity linked” — paid under a separate scheme tied to the department’s work. The railway amount is the same as last year. Other central staff have no such scheme, so they get the Finance Ministry’s 30-day “ad-hoc” bonus.
 Who does not get it
 Group A and gazetted Group B officers — not covered by any of the orders.
 Staff already under a productivity-linked bonus do not also get the Finance Ministry’s 30-day bonus.
 Service condition: you must have been in service on 31 March 2026 with at least six months’ continuous service in the year. Those with six months to a full year get a proportionate share — exactly six months comes to ₹3,454 on our working.
 Casual labour qualify only after three straight years of at least 240 days’ work a year (206 days in five-day-week offices).
 When will the money come?
 The Finance Ministry’s order sets no date for crediting the bonus; departments pay it from their 2026-27 budgets. ESIC has asked its offices to finish payment within 5 working days of its memorandum.
 What about private jobs?
 Bonus for workers in private factories and shops is set by law, not by a government order — at least 8.33% and at most 20%, payable for this year by 30 November 2026. Full details here .
 Check your own bonus for your months of service with our bonus calculator .
 Source: Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) O.M., 15 October 2026; Ministry of Railways PIB release, 14 October 2026; Department of Posts order, 16 October 2026; ESIC O.M., 17 October 2026.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
